questions.enonce_markdown:
Write short notes on the following biological terms.

(i) Stimulus.

(ii) Tropism.

(iii) Reflex action.

(iv) Effector. *(4, 4, 4, 2 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Stimulus**: a **change in the external or internal environment** of an organism that is **detected by a receptor and may cause a response**. Examples: light, heat, sound, touch, chemicals, gravity, pain.

(ii) **Tropism**: a **growth movement of a part of a plant in response to a stimulus coming from one direction**. If the growth is towards the stimulus it is **positive**, away from it **negative**. Examples: phototropism (response to light; shoots are positively phototropic), geotropism (gravity; roots are positively geotropic, shoots negatively), hydrotropism (water), thigmotropism (touch, e.g. tendrils). It is controlled by plant growth substances (auxins).

(iii) **Reflex action**: a **rapid, automatic (involuntary) response to a stimulus, which does not involve the conscious part of the brain**. Its purpose is protection. The pathway (reflex arc) is: stimulus $\rightarrow$ receptor $\rightarrow$ sensory neurone $\rightarrow$ relay (intermediate) neurone in the spinal cord $\rightarrow$ motor neurone $\rightarrow$ effector $\rightarrow$ response. Examples: withdrawing the hand from a hot object, blinking, the knee jerk, sneezing, the pupil constricting in bright light.

(iv) **Effector**: a **muscle or a gland** that **responds to a nerve impulse** from the motor neurone (or to a hormone) by contracting (muscle) or secreting (gland), carrying out the response.

questions.enonce_markdown: With the aid of a diagram, describe the effect of illuminating a shoot from one direction. *(6 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Effect: phototropism.** When a shoot is lit from **one side only**, it **grows (bends) towards the light**: it is **positively phototropic**.

**Diagram (to be drawn):** a shoot (seedling) with light arrows coming from the right; the shoot tip bent towards the right; labels: light direction, shoot tip (coleoptile tip) where auxin is made, shaded side with more auxin and longer cells, lit side with less auxin and shorter cells, region of elongation, direction of curvature.

**Description of the mechanism:**
1. The **tip of the shoot** makes the growth hormone **auxin (indoleacetic acid, IAA)**, which moves down to the zone of elongation.
2. When the light is **from one side**, the auxin **moves (or is redistributed) to the shaded side** of the shoot (light destroys auxin or pushes it away on the lit side).
3. The shaded side therefore has a **higher concentration of auxin**, which makes its cells **elongate more** than those of the lit side.
4. The shoot **bends towards the light** because the shaded side grows faster. The leaves are then better placed to absorb light for **photosynthesis**, which is the advantage of the response.
5. If the tip is removed or covered with foil, no bending occurs; if the light is from above or the shoot is rotated on a klinostat, it grows straight.
